summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of hypercoagulable state, chronic anticoagulation with Lovenox, stable aortic arch thrombus, and chronic chest and abdominal pain was admitted for worsening pain. The chest pain was pleuritic in nature and non-cardiac, with normal cardiac enzymes and EKG. Abdominal pain was diffuse and severe, and on examination, a new incisional hernia was identified. Surgery recommended outpatient management. Pain was controlled with IV morphine initially, then transitioned to oral oxycodone with acetaminophen. The patient's hemoptysis and tracheobronchomalacia remained stable. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with surgery for hernia repair, continue all chronic medications, use temporary increased oxycodone for pain, and evaluate a persistent dental issue with a dentist.
problems: Incisional hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Unspecified disorder of the teeth and supporting structures
Embolism and thrombosis of thoracic aorta
Other diseases of trachea and bronchus
